title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 120 (Maintenance and inspection of documents in electronic form)

content.overview: Without prejudice to other provisions of the Companies Act, section 120 permits documents, records, registers, minutes or books required to be kept by a company, and documents/records allowed to be inspected or copied under the Act, to be kept, inspected or copied in electronic form, as applicable, in the prescribed form and manner.
content.glance: Without prejudice to other provisions of the Companies Act, section 120 permits documents, records, registers, minutes or books required to be kept by a company, and documents/records allowed to be inspected or copied under the Act, to be kept, inspected or copied in electronic form, as applicable, in the prescribed form and manner.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 120 (Electronic form). Without prejudice to other provisions of the Act, documents, records, registers, minutes or books required to be kept by a company, and documents or records allowed to be inspected or copied by a person under the Act, may be kept, inspected or copied, as applicable, in electronic form in the prescribed form and manner. Section 120 changes the permitted form; it does not remove the underlying record-keeping duty, expand inspection rights beyond the Act, or excuse compliance with rules governing the particular record. The topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Records maintained electronically
sections.body: Documents, records, registers, minutes or books of any type required to be kept by a company under the Act may be kept or maintained in electronic form in the prescribed form and manner.

sections.heading: Inspection and copies
sections.body: Where the Act allows a document or record to be inspected or a copy to be given to a person, the inspection or copy may, as applicable, be provided in electronic form in the prescribed form and manner.

sections.heading: Relationship with other provisions
sections.body: Section 120 operates without prejudice to other provisions of the Act. Electronic form does not remove the underlying duty to keep a record or expand the persons entitled to inspect or obtain copies.

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 120 (Maintenance and inspection of documents in electronic form)

examples.title: Electronic register inspection
examples.body: Where a person is legally entitled under the Act to inspect a register or obtain a copy, check the applicable prescribed rules for providing the inspection or copy in electronic form.

hypotheticals.question: A company keeps a register electronically, but an entitled person requests inspection or a copy. What does section 120 cover?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 120 covers not only electronic maintenance but also electronic inspection or copies, as applicable, for documents or records that the Act allows to be inspected or copied. The form and manner remain subject to the prescribed requirements and the person's underlying entitlement.

misconceptions.trap: Reading section 120 as allowing only electronic storage, not electronic inspection or copies.
misconceptions.correction: The section expressly covers electronic form for keeping, inspection or copies, as applicable, in the prescribed form and manner.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming electronic form expands who may inspect a record or receive a copy.
misconceptions.correction: Section 120 does not independently expand inspection rights; the underlying Act provision determines entitlement.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 120 permit?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Specified documents, records, registers and minutes may be maintained and inspected in electronic form in the prescribed manner. Underlying record-keeping and inspection duties remain.

examTips: Explain that electronic form is conditional on the prescribed manner.
Distinguish form of a record from the underlying duty to keep or disclose it.
revisionPoints: Section 120 covers electronic maintenance and, where applicable, inspection or copies.
The prescribed form and manner apply.
Underlying record-keeping duties and inspection entitlements remain governed by the Act.
